metadata.name: [GCP Cloud SQL SQL Server OTel] HA failover occurred or standby unavailable
metadata.description: Alerts when a high-availability (regional) SQL Server instance requested an automatic failover in the last 15 minutes, or its latest available_for_failover sample is 0 (the standby cannot take over), for 2 consecutive checks. Both metrics are reported only for HA instances, so zonal instances never alert. Applies the SQL Server engine marker. Grouped by database_id.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.cloudsql_sqlserver.otel-*
| WHERE gcp.resource_type == "cloudsql_database"
// Resolve per minute first (fragmentation-safe).
// available_for_failover (GAUGE, > 0 = standby ready) and auto_failover_request_count
// (DELTA) are reported only for HA (regional) instances; zonal instances never alert.
| STATS failover_ready = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/available_for_failover`)),
        failovers = SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/auto_failover_request_count`)),
        ss = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/sqlserver/memory/page_life_expectancy`))
    BY `@timestamp` = TBUCKET(1 minute), database_id
// SQL Server engine marker: excludes MySQL / PostgreSQL HA instances
| INLINE STATS ss_total = SUM(ss) BY database_id
| WHERE ss_total > 0 AND (failover_ready IS NOT NULL OR failovers IS NOT NULL)
| EVAL ready_ts = CASE(failover_ready IS NOT NULL, `@timestamp`, NULL)
| STATS failover_ready = LAST(failover_ready, ready_ts),
        ready_minutes = COUNT(failover_ready),
        failovers = SUM(failovers)
    BY database_id
| EVAL failovers = COALESCE(failovers, 0)

breach.segment:
// Breach when either:
//  - an automatic failover was requested in the window (the primary failed over), or
//  - the latest readiness sample says the standby cannot take over (HA protection lost).
WHERE failovers > 0 OR (ready_minutes > 0 AND failover_ready == 0)
| EVAL reason = CASE(
    failovers > 0 AND failover_ready == 0, "automatic failover occurred; standby not ready",
    failovers > 0, "automatic failover occurred",
    "standby not available for failover")
| KEEP database_id, reason, failovers, failover_ready
| SORT database_id
| LIMIT 100

data.content:
## Cloud SQL for SQL Server HA failover occurred or standby unavailable

For a regional (HA) instance, either an automatic failover was requested (the primary zone failed and the standby took over), or the standby is currently not available for failover, so the next zonal failure becomes an outage.

### Triage
1. `automatic failover occurred`: check the Cloud SQL operations log and Google Cloud status page for the zone. Applications saw a brief outage and reconnects; confirm they recovered. Check restart and instance-down alerts for the same instance.
2. `standby not available for failover`: often temporary during maintenance, a recent failover (standby rebuilding) or heavy write load. If it persists, open a support case.
3. Open the Instance Detail dashboard to correlate with CPU, disk and write load.

### Tuning
- To alert only on lost standby readiness, remove `failovers > 0 OR` from the breach filter.
- Increase the alert delay to tolerate longer standby rebuilds after maintenance.

### Behaviour notes
- Healthy: latest available_for_failover > 0 and no failover requests in the window. Breaching: latest readiness = 0 or any failover request (failovers = 1 breaches), for 2 consecutive checks.
- Missing data: zonal (non-HA) instances do not report these metrics and are never evaluated; absence is not treated as unavailability.
